solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Conman to see all over the place? Run inside shelter

indicators.note: things all over the place are scattered, so these letters lose their order
inside says the preceding letters sit within the word for shelter

blocks.note: a bunker is a protective shelter; it is split around the inserted letters
the two words rearranged
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: A trickster who sees too much, running for cover.
explanation.walkthrough: A bunker can be any protective shelter, not just a golf hazard; 'to see' is fodder, not the sense of a conman watching.
explanation.definitionFit: A bunko steerer is American slang for a swindler who lures victims into a crooked game.

clue.text: African people, a considerable come-down when seen going round like this

indicators.note: going round means one word encircles the other

blocks.note: bathos is a ludicrous descent from the elevated to the trivial
so means in this manner

explanation.surface: Some African tribe suffers a serious fall in fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: Bathos is the literary term for an anticlimax, a sudden drop from the sublime to the ridiculous, which is the 'considerable come-down'.
explanation.definitionFit: The Basotho are the Sotho-speaking nation of Lesotho in southern Africa; the plural takes an S.

clue.text: One may be detected in nag, poorly

definitions.text: One may be detected in nag, poorly

indicators.note: poorly suggests something in bad shape, so the word nag is knocked out of order
something detected in another is found inside it

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
an is the indefinite article, meaning one

explanation.surface: A disease might be diagnosed in a sickly old horse.
explanation.walkthrough: AN goes inside a rearranged NAG. Read whole, the clue also defines: a sickly nag may well have this tsetse-borne illness.
explanation.definitionFit: Nagana is the African trypanosome disease of horses and cattle spread by tsetse flies; NGANA is a variant spelling.

clue.text: Asian tree: this arar is cultivated in Karakorum

indicators.note: cultivated ground is turned over, so the letters of the place name are worked into a new order

blocks.note: a Central Asian mountain range, taken whole
the arar is a North African tree; its letters are taken away

explanation.surface: A tree is grown in a remote Asian mountain region.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: the answer plus ARAR rearranges to KARAKORUM, so remove ARAR's letters and KOKUM remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Kokum is an Indian tree of the mangosteen family, whose fruit gives a souring agent and kokum butter.

clue.text: A sad peer, legs collapsing, falls flat

indicators.note: something collapsing falls into disorder, so these letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the fodder, all twelve letters

explanation.surface: A miserable lord whose legs give way tumbles over.
explanation.definitionFit: To spreadeagle is to sprawl with limbs outstretched, as someone who has fallen flat on the ground.

clue.text: Acid converter Sam and Ian adapted to penetrate Jock's through passage

indicators.note: adapted means altered, so the two names are reworked
to penetrate is to get inside something else

blocks.note: transe is a Scots word for a passage or corridor; Jock stands for a Scot
the name taken as written
the name taken as written

explanation.surface: Two Scotsmen alter something to get through a corridor.
explanation.walkthrough: The jumbled SAM and IAN sit inside TRANSE, after its fifth letter. 'Jock' is crossword shorthand for a Scotsman.
explanation.definitionFit: A transaminase is an enzyme that transfers amino groups, converting one amino acid into another.

clue.text: Consent for digging into eastern mineral, causing blot on the landscape?

indicators.note: digging into something puts you inside it

blocks.note: E is the abbreviation for eastern
yes gives consent
ore is a mineral that is mined

explanation.surface: Permission to mine in the east produces an ugly scar on the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: YES burrows into E plus ORE.
explanation.definitionFit: An eyesore is something unsightly, the stock phrase for which is a blot on the landscape.

clue.text: Deliveries not properly secure with end of services

indicators.note: not properly means wrongly arranged, so the word secure is mixed up
end of picks out only the final letter of the following word

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged
the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: Packages arrive insecurely at the close of a church service.
explanation.definitionFit: To deliver someone is to save them from danger, so deliveries in that old sense are acts of saving.

clue.text: Head welcomes married beaks

indicators.note: to welcome is to take someone in, so one word goes inside the other

blocks.note: ras is a headland or cape
M is the abbreviation for married; the answer also lurks backwards in 'welcomes married', a coincidence the setter does not use

explanation.surface: A headteacher greets newly-wed magistrates.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Beaks' looks like slang for magistrates or teachers, but here it means the battering prows of ships.
explanation.definitionFit: A ram is the projecting beak on the prow of a warship used to strike enemy vessels.

clue.text: Star group, first of records appearing in past

indicators.note: first of keeps only the opening letter of the next word
appearing in something places it inside

blocks.note: ago means in the past
the initial letter

explanation.surface: A band of celebrities whose early records belong to the past.
explanation.definitionFit: Argo is the large southern constellation named after Jason's ship, now divided into smaller ones.

clue.text: Branching like a rose?

blocks.note: first meaning: forming sprigs, like a spray of foliage
second meaning: giving out fine droplets, as the perforated nozzle of a watering can does

explanation.walkthrough: The rose here is not the flower but the sprinkler head on a watering can or shower; one word covers both the twiggy and the misty sense.
explanation.definitionFit: A spray is both a small flowering branch and a mist of droplets, so the adjective serves both senses.

clue.text: Tent party our troop's holding

indicators.note: holding means the run of words keeps the entry within its letters

blocks.note: the letters straddling the three words

explanation.surface: Our scout troop's group is carrying a tent.
explanation.definitionFit: A yourt, more often spelt yurt, is the circular felt tent of Central Asian nomads.

clue.text: Cap with a plume has twisted end in ring, often

indicators.note: twisted means bent out of shape, so the word has gets rearranged

blocks.note: the three letters rearranged
a knockout is how a boxing bout in the ring often finishes

explanation.surface: A plumed hat with a bent tip often ends up in the ring.
explanation.walkthrough: KO is the standard abbreviation for a knockout.
explanation.definitionFit: A shako is a tall cylindrical military hat with a peak and usually a plume or pompom.

clue.text: Fie! Stop holding artillery up

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the letters read from bottom to top
holding means one word clasps the other inside it

blocks.note: ho is an old call to halt
RA, the Royal Artillery, turned round

explanation.surface: An outraged cry demanding the guns be held back.
explanation.walkthrough: RA stands for the Royal Artillery, a regiment of the British Army.
explanation.definitionFit: Haro is an old exclamation of outrage or a call for help, comparable to 'shame!' or 'fie!'.

clue.text: Cleansing agent essential for robe sometimes

indicators.note: essential means at the core, so the entry lies inside the following words

blocks.note: the letters bridging the two words

explanation.surface: A detergent one sometimes needs for washing a gown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleansing agent' suggests soap, but it is a sweeping tool.
explanation.definitionFit: A besom is a broom made of twigs, and a broom cleans by sweeping.

clue.text: Surface of liquid: scum stirring without rolling in it

indicators.note: stirring a liquid mixes it, so the word scum is jumbled
something rolling turns over, so the letters run backwards
in it means placed inside the earlier jumbled word

blocks.note: the four letters rearranged and split around the insert
sine is Latin for without, here turned round

explanation.surface: Froth on a liquid is stirred, but not by someone wealthy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rolling in it' reads as being rich, but 'rolling' turns SINE round and 'in it' puts it inside the jumbled SCUM.
explanation.definitionFit: A meniscus is the curved upper surface of a liquid in a tube, caused by surface tension.

clue.text: Steamer to enclose securely, containing small piece of mutton

indicators.note: a small piece of a word is just its opening letter
containing means the first word holds the next one inside

blocks.note: to trap is to shut something in
the initial letter

explanation.surface: A cook seals a scrap of mutton inside a steamer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Steamer' suggests a cooking pot, but it is a ship.
explanation.definitionFit: A tramp is a cargo steamship with no fixed route, picking up freight wherever it can.

clue.text: Green type of bean in home-made bottle?

blocks.note: a green light means go
urd is an Indian bean, black gram

explanation.surface: An unripe variety of bean kept in a homemade jar.
explanation.definitionFit: A dried gourd shell is hollowed out and used as a rustic water bottle; the question mark admits it is grown, not made.

clue.text: Clubbing Yankee to study hard about sonic dancing

indicators.note: dancing letters move about, so the word sonic is rearranged
about means going round the other part

blocks.note: dig is American slang for studying hard; Yankee flags the US usage
the five letters rearranged

explanation.surface: An American student swots with loud music playing for a night out.
explanation.definitionFit: Discoing is going out dancing at discos, which is what clubbing means.

clue.text: Prince historically cut dash with poor

indicators.note: cut means chopped up, so the following letters are reshuffled

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A historic prince made a splash in front of the poor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cut dash' parodies the phrase 'cut a dash'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hospodar was the title of the governing princes of Wallachia and Moldavia under Ottoman rule.

clue.text: Like kings of old, shocked time is wasted

indicators.note: wasted means lost or squandered, so that letter disappears from the word

blocks.note: startled means shocked
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Monarchs of the past were startled that time was squandered.
explanation.walkthrough: Remove one T from STARTLED.
explanation.definitionFit: Starled is a rare old adjective for adorned with stars, as royal regalia and orders of chivalry were.

clue.text: Capped arms stacked and put away

blocks.note: to pile arms is to stack rifles together; the fragment is that stock phrase
to put away food is to eat it

explanation.surface: Weapons were heaped up and stored, then topped off.
explanation.definitionFit: Pileate means having a pileus or cap, as a mushroom or a crested bird does.

clue.text: Nog I mixed with this? Something maybe that one shouldn't drink

definitions.text: Nog I mixed with this? Something maybe that one shouldn't drink

indicators.note: mixed means blended together, so the letters combine in a new order

blocks.note: the result of the mix, taken whole
these letters are removed from the result

explanation.surface: A warning about spiking an eggnog with something undrinkable.
explanation.walkthrough: A composite anagram: NOG I plus the answer rearrange to SOMETHING, so take NOGI's letters away. Read whole, the clue defines a spirit nobody should drink.
explanation.definitionFit: Meths, methylated spirits, is industrial alcohol made poisonous and undrinkable on purpose.

clue.text: Screen filled with e.g. locust storms

indicators.note: filled with means the first word holds the next one inside it

blocks.note: tems is an old word for a sieve, something that screens
a locust is an example of a pest

explanation.surface: A screen swarming with locusts, as in a biblical plague.
explanation.definitionFit: Tempests are violent windstorms, so the plural noun matches.

clue.text: Charge for grinding, sound as a bell

blocks.note: first meaning: the share of grain a miller took as payment
second meaning: to ring slowly and steadily

explanation.walkthrough: 'Sound as a bell' looks like the idiom for perfectly healthy, but here sound is a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a levy or payment, historically the miller's portion, and the measured ringing of a bell.

clue.text: Pod? Get —— apt to burst yielding last peas

indicators.note: something that bursts flies apart, so the letters are scattered into a new order

blocks.note: the result of the mix, taken whole
these letters are removed from it

explanation.surface: Splitting a pea pod to get the last of the peas out.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash stands for the answer: it plus APT rearranges to LAST PEAS, so remove APT. 'Pod' is not the pea's case but a group of sea mammals.
explanation.definitionFit: A pod is the collective noun for a group of seals, whales or dolphins.

clue.text: Maître d', one giving men orders for wine

blocks.note: Me is the French abbreviation of the title Maître
the letter taken as written
OC is the officer commanding

explanation.surface: A head waiter, a commanding type, takes the orders for wine.
explanation.walkthrough: Maître d' looks like the restaurant head waiter, but it splits: Me is how French writes the lawyer's title Maître.
explanation.definitionFit: Médoc is a red Bordeaux wine from the district of that name on the Gironde.

clue.text: Girl's heading for oblivion right to the end

indicators.note: heading for picks out the front letter, which then travels elsewhere
right to the end says that front letter moves all the way to the back

blocks.note: Lethe is the river of forgetfulness in the Greek underworld

explanation.surface: A girl is heading for complete oblivion.
explanation.walkthrough: Move the first letter of LETHE to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Ethel is a woman's given name, and crosswords use girl to signal a female first name.

clue.text: Simple garment I had lifted, feeling sexy inside

indicators.note: in a down entry, lifted means the letters are read upwards
inside means the feeling sits within the other letters

blocks.note: I'd, short for I had, turned round
hot means sexually aroused

explanation.surface: Someone hitched up a plain garment while feeling amorous.
explanation.definitionFit: A dhoti is the plain loincloth wrapped round the waist worn by Hindu men, a single length of cloth.

clue.text: The old grip tightly, steering wildly

indicators.note: wildly means out of control, so the word steering goes haywire

blocks.note: the fodder, all eight letters

explanation.surface: An old driver clutching the wheel tightly but swerving all over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The old' marks an archaic word; here Spenser's spelling of strain.
explanation.definitionFit: Streigne is Spenser's form of strain, in its sense of clasping or squeezing tightly.

clue.text: W. African folk sun looks down on usually

indicators.note: in a down entry, one part looking down on another sits above it

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for sun
usu. is the dictionary abbreviation for usually

explanation.surface: West African people whose sun usually shines down on them.
explanation.definitionFit: The Susu are a Mande-speaking ethnic group of Guinea and Sierra Leone in West Africa.

clue.text: Cavalryman partaking in final hurrah, but forced to retreat

indicators.note: partaking in means taking a share of the following words, so the entry sits within them
a retreat goes backwards, so the letters read from right to left

blocks.note: the letters bridging the two words

explanation.surface: A horseman joins a last charge but is driven back.
explanation.definitionFit: An uhlan was a lancer in the Polish, Prussian or Austrian cavalry.

clue.text: Part of Indira's getup, a little cold before her local festival?

blocks.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
Holi is the Hindu spring festival of colours, local to an Indian woman like Indira

explanation.surface: An Indian woman, slightly chilly, dresses for her festival.
explanation.definitionFit: A choli is the short fitted blouse worn under a sari, so it forms part of an Indian woman's outfit.

clue.text: Establishment senses stirring around core of proletariat

indicators.note: the core of a word is its central letter
stirring mixes things up, so the word senses is rearranged
around means wrapping the other letter

blocks.note: the six letters rearranged and split around the insert
the sixth of eleven letters

explanation.surface: The Establishment senses unrest among the workers.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Establishment' looks like the ruling class, but it means the state of being settled.
explanation.definitionFit: Setness is the quality of being fixed or settled, a state of being firmly established.

clue.text: David's tangled with one? Vast indeed!

definitions.text: David's tangled with one? Vast indeed!

blocks.note: surface reading: someone has had a scuffle with David
setter's reading: the biblical David fought Goliath, a creature of enormous size

explanation.walkthrough: David here is the shepherd boy who slew Goliath; 'one' is the kind of being he fought, confirmed as huge.
explanation.definitionFit: Eten is an archaic word for a giant, and Goliath is the most famous giant David faced.

clue.text: Anti-corrosion treatment in the main embraced by junior employee

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside the arms of the following word

blocks.note: an underling is a subordinate
the main is a poetic name for the open sea

explanation.surface: A junior worker is mostly occupied with rust-proofing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In the main' reads as mostly, but the main is the sea.
explanation.definitionFit: Undersealing is coating a vehicle's underside with a protective layer to stop rust.
